reflections.summary: The rain core was hard-countered by Altaria's Cloud Nine negating Drizzle, leaving Swampert-Mega at base 104 Speed (slower than Floette-Mega 107+) whenever weather dropped. Swampert entered at 48% already damaged from the unseen early turns, and Rotom-W cleaned up by Thunderbolting Pelipper and Hydro Pumping Swampert. The four brought (Pelipper/Swampert/Gholdengo/Incineroar) had no answer to Rotom-W and no way to maintain rain through Cloud Nine, so the Mega Swampert plan was unsuited to this op
reflections.adjustment: Either lead aggressively to eliminate Altaria before committing to rain, or swap the four-pick to avoid full rain dependency. If keeping Swampert-Mega, bring a dedicated Rotom-W answer (e.g., a Grass-type or special wall) instead of Gholdengo, and ensure Swampert enters at high HP. Consider not bringing Pelipper if Altaria's Cloud Nine can repeatedly strip rain.

Plan for g2: if keeping rain, KO Altaria first and pack a Rotom-W switch-in; otherwise pivot away from Swampert-Mega as the intended Mega.

reflections.summary: I was able to systematically eliminate each of my opponent's threats by capitalizing on favorable type matchups and leveraging Protect to waste their offensive turns. Rotom-Wash's Electric and Water coverage, combined with Floette-Mega's Fairy Aura-boosted Moonblast, allowed me to trade efficiently and maintain board control in the Rain, ultimately leaving my Rotom-Wash unchallenged.
reflections.adjustment: For the next game, consider leading Rotom-Wash and a dedicated Gholdengo answer, as the opponent's Gholdengo proved fragile but threatening. Also, be prepared to deny or stall Trick Room from Farigiraf, as the opponent may lead with it more aggressively after struggling to set up in Game 1.
